judge_assessment.explanation: I re-solved all ten problems from the diagrams in worksheet.tex and agree with the judge's mathematics: one juice box = 10/2 = 5 cups so soda = 15 (p1); 4 laps : 6 min gives 12, 18 and 15 minutes (p2); 48 cm over 8 boxes = 6, red 18, blue 30 (p3); 12/3 = 4 dollars per kg and 28 for 7 kg (p4); 4/5 = 0.80 against 6/8 = 0.75 (p5); 3x = 12 so x = 4, 16 walkers and 28 riders (p6); 375 km and 4 hours (p7); 8 pages a minute and 7.5 minutes (p8); 2/5 = 0.4 against 3/7 = 0.4286 (p9); 24x = 120 so x = 5 kg and 15/24 = 0.625 kg per person (p10). The diagrams are load-bearing, as the judge says -- problem 6's tape really does encode the three-box difference. But visual_and_print and answer_key_quality both scored 4, and the delivered key's Quick Answers bank prints '5. 0.8, 0.75, --' and '9. 0.4, --'. Both dashes are verified compare relations ('>' and '<'), and since this sheet has no manual items at all, three of the answers a grader most needs -- which pen is cheaper, which recipe is sweeter -- are simply absent from the bank. Problem 9 also asks for each ratio 'as a fraction of flour' while the verify entry and the boxed key answer give the decimal 0.4, and recipe Y's 3/7 has no entry at all (the key only approximates it as 0.43).

strengths_to_preserve: Every problem carries a drawn tape diagram or double number line that the solution actually needs. Problem 6 is the clearest: the walk tape is 4 boxes, the ride tape 7, and the 12 extra students are the three boxes that stick out -- the equation 3x = 12 is read off the picture rather than imposed on it. That is the representations-applications mode done properly.

Problem 10 makes the synthesis genuinely two-part: solve a proportion off the double number line for x = 5 kg, then give the unit rate 0.625 kg per person, and the key closes with a check that both pairs lie on one line (0.625*8 = 5 and 0.625*24 = 15).

The grading notes name the specific wrong move rather than the wrong number: 'dividing 48 by 3 or by 5 is the classic error -- the known total covers all the boxes, not one colour's boxes' (p3), and 'B is cheaper because 6 is less than 8 compares the wrong things' (p5).

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt() sympifies string expecteds and returns '---' when sympify raises, so every verified relation vanishes from the bank. On this sheet the relation IS the answer for problems 5 and 9.
evidence: verify.json id 5 compare [0.8, 0.75] expected '>' and id 9 compare ['2/5', '3/7'] expected '<', both passing (gate_log verify-ws PASS, 24 tagged checks)
scripts/render_quick_answers.py lines 56-61 return '---' on SympifyError; lines 71-73 return the same '---' for a manual-only id
This sheet has zero manual entries, so every '--' in its bank is a check that passed and was then thrown away

root_causes.description: Problem 9 prints four responses -- X's ratio as a fraction, Y's ratio as a fraction, the relation, and the name of the sweeter recipe -- against two verify entries, and the one numeric entry is in the wrong form: the question asks for a fraction and `expected` is 0.4.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 9: 'Write each ratio as a fraction of flour, compare them with > or <, and name the sweeter recipe.'
verify.json id 9: eval a/b = 0.4 and compare ['2/5','3/7'] -> '<'; no entry for 3/7 as a value and none for the named recipe
answer_key.pdf p3 boxes '0.4' for X and only approximates Y ('3 / 7 ~ 0.43'), so the requested fraction form is never the boxed answer
Problem 5 has the same shape: the printed 'name the cheaper brand' answer has no entry

improvements.title: Render the verified > and < in the Quick Answers bank
improvements.proposed_change: Teach the Quick Answers bank to render a verified relation. In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, render_entry() should special-case an entry whose type is 'compare' with order 'relation': build the line from the entry's own `values` and `expected`, e.g. `$34 < 34.2$`, instead of handing the bare string '<' to _fmt(). _fmt() must stop returning '---' for a relation token, and '---' must remain reserved for items that carry no `expected` at all (genuine manual review), so the two states are visually distinct on the page.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_render_quick_answers.py gains this case's id 5: entries [eval 0.8, eval 0.75, compare values [0.8, 0.75] expected '>']. Assert the rendered line contains '0.8 > 0.75' and no '---'. render_entry returns '0.8, 0.75, ---' today, so the assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The bank stops hiding the answer to the two comparison problems on this sheet, and '---' recovers its meaning as 'no machine check exists' rather than 'the check was a relation'.
improvements.risk: Low; the change touches one formatting path. Compile the fixture key in the test so a math-mode escaping slip cannot reach a delivered PDF.

improvements.title: Answer problem 9 in the fraction form the question asks for
improvements.proposed_change: Set verify.json id 9's first expected to the exact rational '2/5' rather than 0.4, add the missing entry for recipe Y ('3/7'), and let the key box the fractions it asked the student to write. More generally, add a form check to tests/check_prose_consistency.py: when a problem's printed text requests an answer 'as a fraction' or 'in simplest form', a float `expected` on that id is a failure -- SymPy Rational round-trips through verify.py's safe_parse, so the exact form is always available.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_pipeline_fixes.py gains a fixture pairing the printed text 'Write each ratio as a fraction of flour' with a verify entry whose expected is 0.4. Assert the prose checker exits non-zero; change the expected to '2/5' and assert exit 0. The checker has no form rule today, so the first assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: A student told to write 2/5 is graded against 2/5, and the bank stops printing a decimal where the sheet asked for a fraction. It also closes the smaller gap that recipe Y's ratio is only ever approximated in the key.
improvements.risk: The cue phrases are English-specific and could miss 'leave your answer as a ratio'. Start with the two explicit phrases the skill already uses in its directions and extend from observed failures.

improvements.title: Cover the uncovered fraction and the two name-the-winner slots
improvements.proposed_change: Extend the sheet-side gate so coverage is counted per printed response slot, not per problem id. tests/check_answer_line.py already segments the worksheet and reads verify.json; have it also count the response slots each segment prints (\ansblank, \answerline, \ansline, and \underline{\hspace{...}}) and fail when a problem prints more slots than its id has verify entries, unless the surplus is explicitly absorbed by a 'manual' entry. SKILL.md's JSON-format section should state the rule as 'one check per printed blank', replacing today's 'at least one check per problem id'.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_unit_binding.py gains a fixture from problem 9: a segment requesting two fractions, a relation and a named recipe against a verify.json id 9 with two entries. Assert check_answer_line.py exits 1 naming the shortfall; add the 3/7 entry and a read_data lookup for the named recipe and assert exit 0. No slot count exists today, so the first assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: Problems 5 and 9 stop shipping printed answers ('Brand B', 'Recipe Y', 3/7) that no check ever touched, on a sheet whose whole point is comparing two ratios.
improvements.risk: Name answers need read_data string lookups rather than expressions; keep the lookup table derived from the problem's own givens so it does not become a second source of truth.

case_summary: A 32/32 representation-first ratio sheet, and it deserves most of that: ten problems each built on a tape diagram or double number line that the solution genuinely uses, every value re-solved here and correct, a synthesis item that solves a proportion off the line and then extracts the unit rate, and grading notes that name the wrong move rather than the wrong number. Two defects survive the perfect score. The Quick Answers bank prints '--' for the verified relations in problems 5 and 9, and since this sheet has no manual items, those dashes delete the only answers to the two comparison problems. Problem 9 also asks for ratios 'as a fraction of flour' while the verified expected is the decimal 0.4, recipe Y's 3/7 has no entry at all, and the two 'name the cheaper/sweeter one' slots are unchecked. The tape label '10 cups in all' on problem 1 sits beside the juice bar only and is disambiguated by the problem text, so I do not treat it as a defect, but a shorter label ('juice: 10 cups') would remove the last chance of misreading it as the two-bar total.
